Thanks! `0x2a603Dbba2500596cE58ED2c5867658cc436795e` <@412614104222531604> https://faucet.zhejiang.ethpandaops.io/ Hello , do we need to be on this latest version of geth client to go through the shangai upgrade? https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/releases/tag/v1.11.0 This is only for sepolia, once we have a mainnet date, we will create a new release thanks. I am interested in goerli and mainnet. I see that the above release involves change from levelDB to pebble. Is that something we can expect with mainnet also? We run archival nodes and syncing from scratch takes weeks to complete. At some point yes, but pebble support is optional at the moment. We will also switch to a path-based storage scheme soon (also optional at first) so you will need to resync at some point in the next year probably But then your archive node will take less space and be faster (hopefully) Will pebble still need pruning? Yes, we need offline pruning at the moment because we don't know at runtime which trie nodes we can safely delete. With PBSS (path-based storage scheme) we know exactly what to prune. Pebble is just a different database implementation, but doesn't change _how_ we store the data <@360491619402776577> when can we expect to get v1.11.0 released for goerli? This will be v1.12.0 and it will be released once we set a date for goerli, probably 2-3 weeks Thanks a lot <@360491619402776577> .. Basic question- how do we know from the release notes that v1.11.0 is specific to sepolia because I could not find a mention of sepolia in the release notes . Thanks Hmm it was in an earlier version of the release notes yeah, current ones are confusing with " but activation of the fork is not configured." Release notes also tease PBSS for 1.12. Are you saying ... PBSS in 2-3 weeks? 😍 I wouldn't bet on it 🙈 Ah damn I misstyped, shanghai for goerli will be on 1.11.1 not 1.12 pbss before cancun? I would hope so A feature similar to Pebble, where it uses PBSS on fresh sync and then detects it on start if present, would be amazing. This makes it trivial to migrate users over without much user interaction other than "I have a DB" or "I deleted my DB" For pebble it was a minimal change to the entrypoint script: if geth/chaindata exists do nothing, if it doesn't exist add the parameter to use Pebble

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: This is only for sepolia, once we have a mainnet date, we will create a new release

excerpts.author: cheerful_piglet_95568
excerpts.content: thanks. I am interested in goerli and mainnet. I see that the above release involves change from levelDB to pebble. Is that something we can expect with mainnet also? We run archival nodes and syncing from scratch takes weeks to complete.

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: At some point yes, but pebble support is optional at the moment. We will also switch to a path-based storage scheme soon (also optional at first) so you will need to resync at some point in the next year probably

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: But then your archive node will take less space and be faster (hopefully)

excerpts.author: tersec
excerpts.content: Will pebble still need pruning?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Yes, we need offline pruning at the moment because we don't know at runtime which trie nodes we can safely delete. With PBSS (path-based storage scheme) we know exactly what to prune. Pebble is just a different database implementation, but doesn't change _how_ we store the data
